messages:
Evan K: Quick sync: I'm proposing an "audit-token" canary model. Local observers can short-circuit bad variants fast, but any promotion to STABLE needs a central short-lived audit token. Thoughts?

Lina M: Makes sense. Local fast-fail for safety, central for global consistency. Need clear TTLs on tokens.

Omar: Suggest observers can act for <=30s without token. Any sustained action >30s requires controller approval. This avoids long split-brain during partitions.

deploy-bot: deploy 3112233445: canary "v5-rapid" rolled to 1% at 14:02 UTC. Hooks: latency/error/quality.

Tess: Per-tenant policies are essential. We should keep a local policy cache: fallback_preference, max_spill_pct, emergency_cutoff. Router resolves tenant from token and applies policy locally.

Jon: Fallback hierarchy proposal: 1) prefix cache, 2) tenant pinned variant, 3) quantized variant, 4) hosted fallback. Each step should emit a distinct telemetry tag.

Lina M: Cache warming: mirror 0.1%-0.2% shadow traffic to new variant and skip long gens. Mark mirrored requests so they don't affect quota.

Evan K: State machine sketch: INIT -> SHADOW -> CANARY -> RAMP -> STABLE. Emergency transitions to ROLLBACK or EMERGENCY_SPILL. Observers can trigger emergency spill locally but controller must persist the state.

Omar: Telemetry contract: every decision emits tenant, variant_from, variant_to, reason_code, sample_output_hash, signal_scores (latency,error,quality). Keep payload small to protect PII.

Tess: Ops runbook snippet: EMERGENCY_SPILL -> pause rollout, scale variant to 0, route affected tenants to pinned variant, snapshot traces and cache keys, page oncall with tenant impact.

Jon: Add cooldown hysteresis: after a spill, block promotions for X minutes and require at least one successful audit token before resuming ramp. Prevents flip-flop.

Evan K: Testing: chaos test killing controller, high inter-region latency, and stale-cache scenario. Also schedule eval-replay against a small prompt set every 10m for quality drift.

Lina M: Action items: Omar -> token TTLs + degraded-mode rules; Jon -> telemetry tags; Tess -> ops playbook draft; Evan -> RFC follow-up with state table.

Evan K: Great. Ill collate and start the RFC. Thanks all :thumbsup:
